learning_objective: 🎯 Explore how biotechnology is actively changing the world through pest-resistant crops, lab-grown life-saving medicines, and the promise of gene therapy!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: We create Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs) to increase crop yield, reduce reliance on chemical pesticides, and enhance nutritional value (like 'Golden Rice', which is rich in Vitamin A).

Scientists took a gene (cry gene) from the bacteria *Bacillus thuringiensis* and put it into cotton. The plant now produces a toxic protein. When a caterpillar eats the leaf, the alkaline pH of its gut activates the toxin, killing the pest!

Previously extracted from slaughtered pigs, human insulin is now made in labs. The American company Eli Lilly created separate DNA sequences for insulin chains A and B, grew them in E. coli, and linked them to create pure human insulin.

A method to correct genetic defects in a child or embryo. Instead of just treating symptoms, a normal, functional gene is delivered directly into the individual's cells to replace a defective one (first done for ADA deficiency).

Animals with altered DNA (mostly mice) are used to study diseases, test vaccine safety, and produce biological products. Biopiracy is the unethical commercial exploitation of biological resources without proper authorization or compensation to the native people.

fun_activity.title: 🧬 The Pro-Insulin Puzzle
fun_activity.instructions: Natural human insulin is created as a 'pro-hormone' with three chains: A, B, and C. But the C-chain is extra baggage! To make the active hormone, the body (and scientists) must snip out the C-chain and bind A and B together with disulfide bonds.

exam_tips: 📌 RNA interference (RNAi) is a vital defense mechanism used to protect tobacco plants from nematode infection by silencing the parasite's specific mRNA.
📌 Be clear on why Bt toxin doesn't kill the bacteria that produces it: it exists as an inactive 'protoxin' that only becomes active in the alkaline pH of an insect's gut.
📌 Know the definition of Biopiracy and give an example (like multinational companies trying to patent traditional Indian Basmati rice or Neem).
quick_recap: ⭐ Over 95% of all existing transgenic animals are mice.
⭐ Gene therapy for ADA deficiency is not perfectly curative unless the functional gene is introduced at the early embryonic stage.
⭐ The Indian Parliament cleared the second amendment of the Indian Patents Bill to handle issues related to biopiracy.
